ai.description: This slender, bright green snake reaches 1.5 meters. It features a distinct, elongated, pointed snout and horizontal pupils. The body is characterized by a thin, whip-like tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Ahaetulla nasuta* is its elongated, pointed snout appendage, which is distinctly longer than the diameter of its eye.
ai.habitat: *Ahaetulla nasuta* inhabits low-to-mid-altitude forests, plantations, and dense scrub vegetation, typically remaining within the canopy or shrub layer of the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Long-nosed Tree Snake is primarily diurnal, using its binocular vision and slender, camouflaged body to ambush small lizards among the canopy foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ahaetulla nasuta* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to a litter of 5–20 live young. Breeding typically occurs throughout the year, peaking before the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ahaetulla nasuta* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, inhabiting forests and plantations from sea level up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
